component: photometry of the two luminous arcs (core + glow): cross-sections, component decomposition, taper, colour, recommended layer stack

coordinate_convention.frame: pixel-index (integer coordinate = pixel centre); add +0.5 for SVG user space on a 1024 viewBox
coordinate_convention.t: signed perpendicular distance from the arc centre-line, in px, along the ellipse OUTWARD normal: t>0 points TOWARD the icon centre (convex side of the arc, the lens between the two arcs); t<0 points AWAY from the icon centre, toward the nearer frame edge (CONCAVE side, where the centre of curvature is)
coordinate_convention.centreline: smoothed ridge points of out/analysis/arc_geometry.json (local cubic in arc length, 81-pt window); residual of the raw ridge points about the smoothed line 0.048px (L) / 0.052px (R)

cross_sections.note: raw bilinear samples of reference.png along the true normal, per channel [t,R,G,B]. No masking applied here: samples can include the other arc (|t|>~gap/2), the central flare/streak (|y-515|<12 or within ~70px of (504.5,515.5)) and the frame stroke; see masks_used.

masks_used.frame: |signed distance to frame centre-line|>14 and inside the frame
masks_used.other_arc: distance to the other arc centre-line > 100 px

core.model: box of width w convolved with a gaussian of sigma sig_edge; fitted per station in the R channel over |t|<=26 together with a cubic pedestal (the pedestal absorbs the glow + flare bloom).

sig_edge_px.note: 0.45-0.75 px over the whole arc => the core is a HARD-EDGED stroke with ordinary anti-aliasing only. There is no perceptible blur on the core itself.

found.fwhm_px: = w to within 0.03px because sig_edge<<w; see the per-station table
found.width_profile: w grows from 5.8px at both tips to 8.5px at mid-height (max near y=600); this is geometry, already reported by the geometry agent, and I confirm it. The two extreme tip stations (y=83-86) hit the fit lower bound of 3.0px because the core there is only 4% coverage - ignore those two; use 5.8px.

colour.method: (a) ratio of screen-un-mixed coverages covR/covG/covB per station: 0.86-0.90 / 1.00-1.02 over y in [140,880]; (b) global scan of the fixed core colour in the full 3-channel screen fit (stage-2): median rms 2.72 / 2.68 / 2.74 / 2.84 for R/G = 0.84 / 0.877 / 0.91 / 0.94 -> 0.877 +- 0.03. B/G = 1.00 and 1.013 are indistinguishable (2.69 vs 2.68).
colour.clipping: the core plateau does NOT clip over most of the arc (peak G 216-250, B 216-252); only inside the flare band (y 470-560) and a handful of stations do G,B reach 254-255. Per-station clipped-sample counts are in stage2_rows[].nclip. So the core colour IS recoverable and it is not pure white: R is 12% below G.

found.peak_coverage: core_a in stage2_rows (0..255 = 0..100% coverage of a #E0FFFF layer screened over the glow)

model.space: screen compositing over black in sRGB CODE space (no linearisation). This is the algebra the reference actually obeys: the same layer amplitudes reproduce the profile from t=0 out to t=300.
model.note: sigma_i and delta_i are GLOBAL (one set for both arcs and every station); only the amplitudes A_i_ch and the background vary along the arc. delta<0 means the glow component is centred on the CONCAVE side of the core, i.e. offset away from the icon centre.

fit_quality.note: median over stations of the uniform-in-t weighted rms over the whole +-320px cross-section, all three channels. 1.3 code values is the compression noise floor measured in flat areas.
fit_quality.band_note: median over the 120 stations with |y-515|>120, per channel [R,G,B]. The model sits at the JPEG noise floor (0.7-3.0) everywhere except the 0-6px core-edge band (6.1/8.7/8.9), where the residual is dominated by sub-pixel centre-line and width error - a 0.3px shift of an 8px hard-edged stroke is worth ~30 code values at t=+-4 - not by the photometry. The 6-20px band (2.3/5.2/5.0) is where the unresolvable core/narrow-glow overlap sits.

alternative_N4.note: 4 terms buy 2.18 -> 1.91 code rms. Not worth the extra layer unless the lead wants it.

asymmetry.definition: outer(concave, t<0) / inner(convex, t>0) ratio of the background-subtracted G channel at matched |t|. Background = median of the G channel at |t| in [230,320] on the outer side. Stations with |y-515|<120 are excluded (central flare), and the inner side is only usable where the other arc is >90px away, which is why the ratio is only measurable toward the tips.
asymmetry.verdict: the glow is decisively brighter and wider on the CONCAVE side of each arc - i.e. on the side AWAY from the icon centre, toward the nearer frame edge. (docs/stage1_findings.md calls that side "concave/centre"; the two are opposite: for the left arc the centre of curvature, and the bright lobe, are both at smaller x than the core, while the icon centre is at larger x.)
asymmetry.model_equivalent: in the fitted model the asymmetry is carried entirely by the three offsets delta = (-3.3, -16.2, -62.1) px: every component is a symmetric gaussian, but centred on the concave side of the core. A centred-gaussian model (delta=0) fits far worse (see law_comparison).

extent.definition: largest |t| at which the 13px-smoothed G channel still exceeds the LOCAL far-field background by 2 / 5 / 10 code values. bg_local is the constant fitted per station in the stage-2 screen fit (it is 4-13 in G, i.e. 1-10 above the darkest interior floor of G=3, and it is what the widest glow term degenerates with beyond |t|~220).

inner_side_px.caveat: at mid-height the inner (convex) side cannot be measured at all: the gap between the arcs is 79-170px, so the two glows and the central flare overlap completely there. The 73px figure is the fitted model evaluated at mid-arc amplitudes; the tip figure is direct.

summary.recommendation: the lead must cover about 210 px on the concave/outer side and about 80 px on the convex/inner side of each arc. Beyond that the arc glow is under 2 code values and is indistinguishable from the diffuse interior field.

taper.note: core_cov = screen coverage of the core layer measured in R (0..1, multiply by 255 and divide by 0.877 to get the #E0FFFF layer amplitude); A1,A2,A3 = [R,G,B] peak amplitudes (code units) of the three glow gaussians.

cos_power_law_all_terms.form: A(theta) = A_apex * cos(theta)^p, theta = the ellipse parameter angle of the station (sin theta = (y-cy)/ry, cos theta = |x-cx|/rx, theta=0 at the apex, +-90deg at the poles). Fitted with the flare band |y-515|<90 excluded.
cos_power_law_all_terms.verdict: GLOW: one closed form covers the whole glow taper. A_G = A_apex*cos^p(theta) fits to 5.0% of peak for the sigma=27 term (better than a gaussian in y, 6.8%, an exponential in flare distance, 8.2%, or a power law in flare distance, 11.8%). The fitted power is NOT the same for the three terms: 2.5-2.6 (sigma 7.2), 2.5-3.0 (sigma 26.9), 4.7-5.5 (sigma 56.6) - the widest lobe is markedly more centrally concentrated than the narrow glow. cos(theta) = |x-cx|/rx = sqrt(1-((y-cy)/ry)^2), so cos^3 = (1-((y-cy)/ry)^2)^1.5. CORE: a completely different shape - the cos^p form fits badly (p=0.9, 15% rms) because the core is a PLATEAU with short ramps: coverage 0.69-0.86 for y in [170,860] and a near-linear fade to zero over the last ~60px (top) / ~80px (bottom) of y. The trapezoid fit is 5.2% and is the right description. WHICH VARIABLE? For the core the trapezoid fits equally well in y (5.2/5.6%), arc length (5.1/5.6%), ellipse parameter angle (5.1/5.5%) and flare distance (5.1/5.6%), and the same is true of the glow (3.1-3.6% in all four). The reference therefore does NOT discriminate between those variables - they are monotone reparametrisations of each other over a single arc. Use y: it is the one SVG can express directly as a linearGradient, and it reproduces the data as well as any other choice.

gradient_stops.note: normalised to each quantity's own maximum; y in pixel-index units (add 0.5 for SVG). core_cov is the coverage of the #E0FFFF core layer measured in R and divided by 0.877; A*G_stops are the G-channel peak amplitudes of glow gaussians 1,2,3. Values inside the flare band (|y-515|<80) are LINEARLY INTERPOLATED across, not measured. Values are clamped to 0 outside the core span (y = 88.3..943.5 for L, 85.7..938.8 for R) and an explicit zero knot is inserted at each end. Station-to-station scatter of a few percent is JPEG noise on the pedestal, not structure: smooth before using if the lead wants monotone stops. NOTE the glow terms do not actually reach zero at the core tips (A1_G, A2_G are still ~9-10 code values at the last measurable station) - the zero knot there is a construction convenience.

law_comparison.method: same 32 stations (y in [150,420] and [610,860], both arcs), same masks, |t| in [8,320], all three channels; global shape parameters, per-station per-channel amplitudes refitted for every family (IRLS-linear in screen density, so no family is favoured by the optimiser). Numbers are uniform-in-t rms in code values over the whole cross-section.
verdict: ASYMMETRY IS THE DOMINANT EFFECT: every centred/symmetric family stalls at ~5.9 code rms no matter how many terms you give it (gauss_sym N=3 5.910, expo_sym N=3 5.917), while a single offset exponential already reaches 4.30 and three offset gaussians reach 2.18. The glow is NOT centred on the core.
With ONE term the profile is broader-tailed than a gaussian: offset power law 4.13 ~ offset exponential 4.30 < offset gaussian 5.14.

With THREE terms every family ties (gauss 2.181, expo 2.176, power 2.199, bilateral gauss 2.150), i.e. the profile is a multi-scale falloff and 3 gaussians span it as well as anything. Since feGaussianBlur is what SVG gives you, use 3 offset gaussians.
The power-law family degenerates: at N=2 its optimum runs to r0=1.4e6 px, n=2.4e4, i.e. the exponential limit r0/n = 58px. So there is no evidence for a genuine 1/r^n tail.

A per-side-sigma (bilateral) gaussian stack fits the same as an offset stack (2.150 vs 2.181) - the two are interchangeable descriptions of the asymmetry; offsets are easier to draw in SVG (shift the glow path inward) and bilateral sigmas are not expressible with one blurred stroke.

background_free_differential.method: per-station-side linear regression of R on G and B on G over |t| in [10,150] (the intercept absorbs the local background, so this is immune to any background error). Median over 185 station-sides, sd across them. Sub-ranges: dR/dG 0.009 (y 160-300), 0.023 (300-450), 0.031 (560-720), 0.058 (720-880); dB/dG 0.94, 1.04, 1.06, 0.99 respectively.

per_term_ratios.note: [p25, median, p75] over stations with |y-515|>90 and fit rms<3.5

glow.recommended_note: R/G = 0.03-0.04, B/G = 1.00-1.05 => the wide glow is essentially pure cyan with a few percent of red and a couple of percent more blue than green. #00FFFF and #0AFFFF are both within the measurement error; #0AFFFF reproduces the measured R:G better at 100+ code levels. The narrow term (sigma 7.2) is NOT pure cyan: its R/G is 0.0-0.1 near the tips and 0.2-0.5 over y in [340,700], i.e. there is a faint WHITE halo on the core (visible directly in the raw pixels: at y=301 the R channel is 12-29 for 4-8px either side of the core while the background R is 2-3). Part of that R excess at mid-height is the central flare bloom, so treat 0.25 as an upper bound for a white halo component and 0.03 as the pure-cyan floor.
glow.B_over_G_summary: median per-term B/G = 1.006 / 0.988 / 1.003 for sigma 7.2 / 26.9 / 56.6; background-free differential dB/dG = 1.008 +- 0.090. So B = G to within 1-2%: the glow is a pure cyan, NOT a blue-shifted cyan. (The apparent B excess in raw pixel ratios - B/G = 1.3-1.6 at G<25 - is entirely the dark-blue background field rgb(2,7,14), not the glow.)

core.plateau_extent_px: the flat top of the core is w-2*sig_edge ~ 4.5-7.3px wide; see core.stations[].w
core.clipping_per_station: core.stations[].peakR (max 219 -> never clipped in R) and glow.rows[].nclip = number of samples at or above 254 in any channel (0 for most stations; 1-12 only within |y-515|<130 and at a few mid-arc stations where G,B peak at 250-255)
core.wing_ratios: in the core wings (|t| = 4-8px, where the core has fallen to 2-40% but the glow is still rising) the measured R:G:B is dominated by the core: e.g. L y=301 t=-4 gives (81,145,153) => R/G 0.56, B/G 1.06; t=0 gives (187,224,222) => R/G 0.836, B/G 0.991. The pure-core ratio 0.877 is only recovered after the cyan glow is un-screened out, which is what the 0.877 number above does.

recommended_stack.compositing: screen over black, in sRGB CODE space (mix-blend-mode:screen on isolated groups, or feBlend mode="screen" with color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"). NOTE: for a single-colour blurred stroke the linearRGB-vs-sRGB choice of feGaussianBlur does not matter (the blur acts on premultiplied colour+alpha, so a monochrome layer keeps its colour and only its alpha is blurred) - but the BLEND space does matter.

layers.name: core
layers.stroke_width: 5.8px at the tips -> 8.5px at mid-height (see core.stations[].w); a constant 7.2px costs ~1.3px of width error at the ends
layers.opacity: core_cov(y)/0.877, i.e. 0 at the tips, 0.79-0.97 over y in [170,860]; gradient_stops[arc].core_stops x core_cov_max/0.877

layers.name: glow1
layers.peak_amplitude_G: 0 at the tips, 45-55 at y=200/810, 95-125 mid-arc (flare-inflated above 65; the arc-only value is ~65*cos^3(theta))

layers.name: glow2
layers.peak_amplitude_G: 0 at the tips, 28-34 at y=200/810, 65 at mid-arc (arc-only cos^3 amplitude 65)

layers.name: glow3
layers.peak_amplitude_G: 0 for |y-515|>310 (y<205 or y>825), rising to 28-34 at mid-arc; tapers as cos^4.7..5.5(theta), i.e. much more centrally concentrated than the other two terms

recommended_stack.how_to_turn_a_gaussian_into_a_stroke: a stroke of width W blurred by sigma_b has the perpendicular coverage profile alpha*0.5*(erf((t+W/2)/(sigma_b*sqrt2)) - erf((t-W/2)/(sigma_b*sqrt2))). Choosing W = 2*sigma gives sigma_b = sigma*sqrt(1-1/3) = 0.8165*sigma and a peak factor of erf(0.866) = 0.7793, so alpha = peak_amplitude/255/0.7793. Any (W, sigma_b) with sigma_b^2 + W^2/12 = sigma^2 works; the numbers used in numeric_check[] are exactly this recipe.
recommended_stack.path_offsets: each glow layer is drawn on a path offset INWARD (toward its own ellipse centre) by |delta|: 3.3, 16.2 and 62.1 px. For an axis-aligned ellipse, offsetting inward by d is well approximated by shrinking the radii: (rx-d, ry-d) about the same centre (exact at the apex; the error is under 4px at the tips for d=62, which is 0.07 sigma and invisible).

two_d_cross_validation.what: both arcs screen-composited from their fitted per-station amplitudes and evaluated on the mirror axis x=504.5, i.e. the one place where the inner (convex) wings of both arcs overlap and where nothing was fitted. Columns: [y, perpendicular distance from each arc, measured R,G,B, model R,G,B].
two_d_cross_validation.verdict: the inner-wing extrapolation is good to 2-7 code values. The sign of the residual is informative and is NOT a glow error: for |y-515|>200 the model is 2-3.5 too BRIGHT because the fitted per-station background (G 5.8-7.3, taken from beside the arc) is larger than the actual dark band between the arcs (G 2-4); for |y-515| in [100,200] the model is 4-7 too DIM because the central flare's broad bloom is not part of my model. Both belong to other components (background field, flare), so the lead should not tune the arc glow to close them.

taper_zero_points.direct_probe: sampling the ellipse BEYOND the last ridge point (L top): the core peak above the local field is 48-20=28 at y=86, 33-20=13 at y=80, 26-19=7 at y=74 and indistinguishable at y=68. So the core light ends at y=70-75 (top) and, by symmetry of the measured profile, y=955-960 (bottom). The geometry agent's amp=0 extrapolation (y=89.7 / 940.4 for L) is the point where the fitted plateau amplitude hits zero; there is a 2-6% tail for another ~15-20px along the arc past that.
taper_zero_points.glow: the glow terms do NOT reach zero at the core tips: at the last measurable station (y=85.6 L / 83.2 R) A1_G is still 8-10 and A2_G 9-10 code values. They cannot be traced further because the local diffuse field in the top corners is itself G=16-20 (versus 6-8 at mid-height), so past the core tip the arc glow is no longer separable from the background field.

taper_top_bottom_asymmetry.note: [value at y=514.85-d, value at y=514.85+d, bottom/top ratio]
taper_top_bottom_asymmetry.verdict: The glow is consistently 0-20% brighter in the bottom half than in the top half at matched |y-514.85| (L: 1.04,1.04,1.10,1.20,1.19 at d=150..350; R: 1.09,1.02,1.04,1.10,1.01). The core is NOT consistent: the left core is 0-9% brighter at the bottom while the right core is 5-16% DIMMER at the bottom. So the taper is symmetric about the ellipse centre y to within +-10-20%, with a weak real preference for a brighter bottom glow. A symmetric taper costs at most ~6 code values of glow (A2_G 28.7 vs 34.5 at d=300) and is a defensible simplification.
